cards.front: Recall a key point about The Design Process
cards.back: A design brief defines the problem — who is the audience, what is the message, what are the constraints.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Design Process
cards.back: The design process is iterative: research, ideas, development, refinement, feedback, revision.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Design Process
cards.back: Mind-mapping and mood boards help generate and organise ideas visually at the start of a project.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Design Process
cards.back: Presenting to a client requires clear rationale — explain design decisions, not just show finished work.

cards.front: What should you know about graphic communication exam tips?
cards.back: Show the FULL JOURNEY — research, thumbnails, roughs, development, final. Annotate at every stage. Explain design DECISIONS — why this typeface, why this colour, why this layout? Show ITERATION.
Understand the problem (e.g. Read brief, identify user needs, constraints)
Gather information (e.g. Product analysis, user research, materials investigation)
Define requirements (e.g. List measurable criteria the design must meet)
Generate ideas (e.g. Mind maps, thumbnails, SCAMPER, mood boards)
Refine best idea (e.g. Modelling, prototyping, testing, refining)
Assess against spec (e.g. Test against each specification point)

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Start designing immediately — research wastes time. Correct: AQA AO1 requires you to DEVELOP ideas through INVESTIGATIONS informed by sources. Without research, your work lacks the contextual understanding that earns marks. Research into existing designs, target audience and context is ESSENTIAL.
Respond to a design brief for a music festival poster. Show your complete design process from initial research and mood boards through idea generation to final design. Annotate each stage.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: The Design Process
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of The Design Process using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

cards.front: The Design Process: Step by Step
cards.back: The design process follows a structured sequence: brief analysis, research, specification, ideation, development, modelling, testing, and final outcome. Each stage builds on the previous one. Professional designers iterate between stages rather than following a rigid linear path. The double diamond model (Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver) is widely used in UK design studios.
